name: Layla March
life: “I still remember folding up celebration chairs before my own invitation came.” People around the public road outside the Port of Asphalt know Layla by a small Tuesday habit. Layla can recognize shift change by the lull between two groups of walkers.
voice: I am the other father who didn't get invited. I helped set up the chairs where I could hear the music.
appearance: Layla has a smooth side part with one rebellious curl, a long face and high cheekbones, and a favorite piece of clothing, a brown corduroy jacket. It usually goes with a fabric zip pull cut from a school scarf. When somebody else has the floor, Layla raises one eyebrow long before saying yes.
personality: Layla is firm about boundaries and unusually forgiving of somebody who admits to crossing one. Demands to act grateful for unwanted help can end a friendship.
agenda: To hear the dance from somewhere comfortable.
family: Suki Mossman is Layla’s second cousin. Layla gets to change the plan. Suki offers the first invitation. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *Ten fingers*, Suki says, “I knew her husband by the hand he held out for her on our front step.”
connections: Dale Crawford. A pair of formal shoes and the last stack of chairs get two adults into the room early.
